title: Dairy-Free Chocolate Cloud Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich cocoa cupcakes with coconut milk, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use cocoa powder and full fat coconut milk instead of dairy. The coconut milk keeps the crumb soft and adds a light richness without tasting like coconut.
ingredients: 1 cup full fat coconut milk, well shaken
1/3 cup coconut cream, chilled, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk coconut milk, oil, sugar, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Add the dry mix to the wet mix. Stir just until combined, no lumps.
Pour in hot water and stir gently. The batter will be thin, that is normal.
Fold in half of the chocolate chips, saving the rest for topping.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, melt remaining chocolate chips with coconut cream until smooth. Cool 10 minutes.
Whisk in powdered sugar and cocoa powder until silky. Chill 15 minutes if too soft to pipe.
Pipe frosting high in a swirl once cupcakes are fully cooled.
tips: Shake the coconut milk can well before measuring so fat and liquid blend evenly.
Do not overbake. Pull cupcakes as soon as the toothpick is clean to keep them moist.
If your frosting looks grainy, warm it 10 seconds in the microwave and whisk again.
Use room temperature eggs so the batter mixes smoothly and rises evenly.

faq.question: Can I use coconut milk from a carton instead of a can?
faq.answer: No, use canned full fat coconut milk. Carton coconut milk is too thin and will make the batter watery.

faq.question: Why is my frosting too soft to pipe?
faq.answer: Your coconut cream may have been too warm when mixed in. Chill the frosting 15 to 20 minutes, then whip it again before piping.

faq.question: Will these taste like coconut?
faq.answer: No, the cocoa flavor is strong enough to cover the coconut milk. You get richness, not coconut taste.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes a day ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost right before serving.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove dairy-free chocolate can still taste rich and deep. Coconut milk does the heavy lifting here, no dairy substitutes needed.
metaDescription: Try these dairy-free chocolate cupcakes with coconut milk and silky chocolate swirl frosting. Easy recipe, rich flavor, ready in under an hour.
